question: What proportion of your typical workday is spent on routine, repetitive digital or clerical tasks?
explanation: Tasks with predictable digital inputs (data entry, copy-pasting, standard replies) are prime targets for automated models.

options.label: Over 70% — Most of my tasks follow predictable templates or scripts
options.note: High vulnerability to immediate workflow automation

options.label: 40% to 70% — A mix of standard workflows and unique problem-solving
options.note: Moderate exposure; routine half can be augmented

options.label: 20% to 40% — Mostly novel challenges with occasional documentation
options.note: Substantial human moat in daily activities

options.label: Under 20% — Almost every day presents unscripted, spontaneous situations
options.note: Highly resilient against algorithmic automation

question: How much does your role require physical tactile manipulation in unstructured real-world environments?
explanation: Robots struggle with chaotic, unstructured physical tasks (climbing varied stairs, touching sensitive human tissue, tactile tool feel).

options.label: Zero — 100% of my work is performed on a laptop, screen, or phone
options.note: Pure digital tasks face the fastest software diffusion curves

options.label: Minimal — Mostly desk work with occasional office hardware or filing
options.note: Physical component is too minor to provide defense

options.label: Moderate — Regular on-site inspections, workshop calibration, or field visits
options.note: Physical presence creates a natural geographic and cost buffer

options.label: Dominant — Heavy hands-on craft, manual therapy, surgery, driving, or farm field work
options.note: Hardware and embodied robotics lag far behind software LLMs

question: Does your work depend on building high-stakes emotional trust, de-escalating human panic, or comforting vulnerable people?
explanation: Biological empathy, moral solidarity, and genuine eye contact cannot be replaced by synthetic avatars.

options.label: Rarely — Interactions are transactional (status inquiries, technical specs, invoices)
options.note: Transactional chats are already resolved by voice/chat bots

options.label: Occasionally — Standard customer service or team project check-ins
options.note: Basic customer relations face AI co-pilot integration

options.label: Frequently — Managing sensitive client anxieties, mentoring team members, or teaching
options.note: Interpersonal emotional trust is highly valued

options.label: Crucial Core — Bedside patient nursing, psychological counseling, crisis negotiation, or bereavement support
options.note: Deep human empathy forms an impregnable defensive moat

question: When producing deliverables (code, documents, designs, analysis), what is the source of your output?
explanation: Regurgitating existing online material is trivial for LLMs; uncovering unpublished primary data or breaking new ground is human domain.

options.label: Summarizing or restructuring existing online information, rules, or boilerplate code
options.note: Generative models produce synthesized summaries in seconds

options.label: Applying standard industry frameworks to customer data
options.note: Can be accelerated 3x with prompt-driven copilot tools

options.label: Synthesizing cross-disciplinary insights and balancing complex corporate tradeoffs
options.note: Architectural judgment remains human-centric

options.label: Uncovering original ground truth (field investigative reporting, breakthrough scientific research, bespoke litigation)
options.note: Primary intelligence discovery cannot be scraped from the web

question: Does Indian law or statutory regulation require your personal certified signature and civil/criminal accountability?
explanation: Sections of Indian law (Companies Act for CAs, Advocates Act for litigators, Medical Council for doctors) mandate human legal liability.

options.label: No — Anyone can execute my tasks without professional accreditation or personal legal risk
options.note: Zero statutory protection against corporate AI replacement

options.label: Internal Only — My work is reviewed by internal company managers, but no government regulatory sign-off
options.note: Enterprise can replace processes if quality assurance holds

options.label: Moderate — Semi-regulated domain with institutional compliance audits
options.note: Regulators require human-in-the-loop audit logs

options.label: Strict Legal Mandate — I hold statutory licenses (Bar Council, ICAI, NMC/MCI) and bear personal legal liability
options.note: Courts and regulators strictly prohibit non-human certification

question: What is the capital substitution economics of your role in India?
explanation: In high-wage IT services, companies save millions replacing workers with AI tokens; in low-wage physical labor, robotic hardware is far too expensive.

options.label: High-cost white-collar role — Software engineering, corporate finance, management consulting
options.note: Companies have intense financial motivation to automate high-salary seats

options.label: Mid-tier formal role — BPO team leader, bank officer, content strategist
options.note: High margin pressure driving seat consolidation

options.label: Entry-level physical or local service — Retail assistant, Kirana helper, delivery partner
options.note: Low wage levels make robotic automation financially unviable in India

options.label: Smallholder or informal sector — Agriculture, artisanal fabrication, local community shopkeeper
options.note: Capital cost barriers insulate these roles for decades

category: AI Tool Adoption in Your Daily Work
question: How frequently do you currently leverage AI assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, Cursor, Midjourney) in your workflow?
explanation: Workers who proactively orchestrate AI tools multiply their output and shift from task executors to systems directors.

options.label: Never — I do not use AI tools at all and don't know how they work
options.note: Severe vulnerability to being outperformed by AI-empowered peers

options.label: Occasionally — Basic Google searches or asking ChatGPT for occasional email drafts
options.note: Surface-level usage without deep workflow integration

options.label: Regularly — Daily prompt workflows for drafting, coding, or data formatting
options.note: Active user capturing significant productivity gains

options.label: Mastery — I orchestrate multi-agent workflows, API automations, and evaluate model outputs critically
options.note: You are directing the technology rather than competing with it

question: How fast can you pivot into adjacent technical, managerial, or specialized domains over the next 12 months?
explanation: Career adaptability is the single strongest predictor of long-term economic resilience.

options.label: Difficult — My skills are narrowly specialized to one legacy software or rigid script
options.note: High risk of skill obsolescence without immediate re-skilling

options.label: Moderate — I can take weekend online courses, but career transition would take 2+ years
options.note: Gradual adaptation window

options.label: High — I have strong fundamental problem-solving skills and learn new tech within weeks
options.note: Strong foundational generalist capacity

options.label: Very High — I have a strong multidisciplinary network, commercial acumen, and thrive in ambiguous environments
options.note: Maximum career antifragility
